what_it_does: Many graph problems — such as finding the fastest route through a network where links only exist at certain times (a 'temporal graph,' like a flight schedule where connections are only valid at specific hours) — require processing nodes in strict time order along chains of connected edges. Because one step must finish before the next can start, these problems are deeply sequential and resist the massive parallelism that GPUs (chips designed to run thousands of operations simultaneously) are built to exploit. TempGraph reorganizes the problem by breaking the graph into independent time-ordered chains and introducing 'shortcut' references between chains to represent cross-chain dependencies without forcing sequential execution. A three-phase cycle — generate candidate work items, activate those whose dependencies are satisfied, compute them — lets many chains make progress at the same time on GPU threads, while the shortcuts handle any remaining coordination. This exposes enough parallelism for GPUs to deliver their full memory-bandwidth and compute throughput.
